name: hologram
title: Hologram
description: A scene played as projected light: a ghost double shimmers off the image, emission lines structure it, a halo spills from bright areas, and everything leans toward its tint. WebGL.
useWhen: A feature should present as a projection rather than as a screen: a sci-fi flavoured reveal, a beat about what is coming.
The scene is high contrast, since only what is bright enough carries through the projection.
You want the projection to materialize on entry: raise intensity from 0 and the scene resolves into light.
avoidWhen: The story is a physical display being watched rather than light standing in the air: use crt-screen.
You want damage rather than projection: use sustained-glitch.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Tint
variables.description: Colour of the projected light. Sets the whole character.

variables.label: Glow
variables.description: Emission strength: light off the edges of shapes and the halo bright areas throw.

variables.label: Ghost
variables.description: How unstable the projection is: how far the doubled image sits from the original and how far scanlines slip sideways.

variables.label: Flicker
variables.description: Depth of the brightness pulse, on a 15-frame cycle with per-frame jitter.

variables.label: Intensity
variables.description: How much of the effect shows. 0 shows the plain scene.

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small label above the number in the scene.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Lower renders faster.
